claims.content: The system provides an interface for browsing and searching auction inventory items by filtering based on criteria such as Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material Type, Brand, and Location.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The system provides an interface for browsing and searching auction inventory items by filtering based on criteria such as Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material Type, Brand, and Location.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: The Customer uses the browse/search capability to apply a selected filter criterion to the auction inventory and is shown the matching products.
scope_contract.start_boundary: The Customer is in the product browse/search context, before any filter/search selection has been made.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The Customer sees the products that match the selected browse/search filter criterion; no subsequent product action is included.
in_scope_actions: Searching/filtering inventory items by selectable criteria such as Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material Type, Brand, and Location
excluded_adjacent_actions: Admin/back-office search by Product ID, Customer Email Address, Schedule Date range, Auction Duration, or other administrative criteria
Placing a bid on a product
Checking out or paying for a product
Viewing downstream product details not part of the search/browse results
variant_dimensions: Selectable filter criteria: Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material Type, Brand, Location, etc.

claims.content: Customer
The system has auction inventory data populated and available for the Auctioneer to access.

Products in the auction inventory are marked as both 'Auction Available' AND 'Auction Eligible' in the JTV enterprise systems, so they are counted in inventory numbers and included in the browseable/searchable inventory.
The Customer browses and searches auction inventory items by filtering based on criteria such as Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material Type, Brand, and Location.
The Customer uses the Endeca or Endeca-like search and navigation capability to browse the auction inventory.

The Customer applies one or more filter criteria (e.g., Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone Type, Material Type, Material Purity, Brand, or Location); the available scrolling list boxes allow multiple filters to be selected simultaneously via the Control key.
After configuring the search parameters, the Customer clicks the 'Find Product' button to execute the search.
The system displays the filtered products that match the selected criteria in a 'Search Results' table; the results include thumbnail images and sortable column headers.

Diverges from Step 1: Instead of starting with Endeca navigation, the Customer accesses the browse/search capability via a Site Map page that lists available Categories (e.g., Jewelry, Gemstones, Collectibles, Watches), Product Types (e.g., Rings, Necklaces, Bracelets), and Gemstone Types (e.g., Tanzanite, Diamond, Ruby) as direct links to specific pages or Endeca results pages.

Diverges from Step 1: The Customer enters product browsing via an SEO-optimized landing page focused on a gemstone type or product type (e.g., 'tanzanite page' or 'Rings page') and uses its direct links to reach pre-filtered product views such as 'all loose tanzanite stones' or 'all tanzanite rings'.
The Customer chooses between 'Items currently online only' and 'All sellable auction inventory' via radio buttons.

Diverges from Step 2: The Customer sets radio-button filters that determine whether results include items with images, without images, with a valid (sellable) location, or without a valid (sellable) location; these combinable options alter the composition of the result set.

Diverges from Step 2: The Customer selects a grouping option from a scrolling list box with options including Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material, Material Purity, Product Group, Brand, Inventory Realm (Red, White), Inventory Aging Bucket, J/G Score, and Ring Size; each grouping option generates corresponding columns in the Results section.
Diverges from Step 4: The Customer switches the product results display between 'List View' and 'Catalog View'.
Diverges from Step 4: The Customer sorts the product results by 'Current Price: low to high' using a dropdown menu.

missing_aspects: Evidence does not support scoping search results; it specifies these options do not impact 'Red status' columns.

claims.content: Diverges from Step 4: If the search returns no matching products (e.g., for a term like 'belly button'), instead of displaying the Search Results table, the system displays a 'No Results Found' page that includes: an apology/message stating no matches were found, a 'Search Tips' section with five suggestions (check typos, remove unnecessary words, try plural/singular forms, use fewer/generic keywords, and contact support), and a 'May We Suggest'/'Popular Searches' section with static lists of popular gemstone and jewelry searches plus dynamically updated search terms/phrases using Omniture data.
Diverges from Step 4: If the Customer clicks a link/category that contains no products (e.g., a collectibles link), the system serves a 'no results found' page.

Diverges from Step 4: Products without an available image are never eligible to appear on search results or catalog pages; this pre-filtering constraint may yield an empty result set even when other search criteria match.

missing_aspects: The evidence does not document the continuation or exit after the 'No Results Found' page (e.g., return to search, terminate, or offer retry).

claims.content: The system displays a table titled 'Search Results' showing the products that match the selected browse/search criteria, with columns in this default order: Action (checkbox), Item thumbnail image, Product ID (SKU #) with link to SKU History page, Auction ID number, Description, Opening Bid, High Bid, Item Unit Cost, Start time (initially blank), End time (initially blank), Duration (initially blank), Product Type, and Increment.

The system displays a filtered product list in which each item is represented by a Product Module containing a thumbnail image, a short description (On-Air Description), a countdown timer in D:HH:MM:SS format showing the time remaining, the current high bid, and a QuickBid button.

citation_audit.description: Latest model-authored candidates after internal semantic grounding verification and DRA; aligned with delivered slots.
